title: Barnabas (11 June)
hookLine: son of encouragement, who vouched for Paul when no one else would

lines: A ROOM FULL OF FRIGHTENED PEOPLE.
A FORMER PERSECUTOR AT THE DOOR.
cards: They were all afraid of him, Acts says. Not long ago he was hunting them, dragging believers out of their houses. Now he has come to Jerusalem saying he met the risen Jesus on the road.
The disciples don't believe he is one of them. Nobody moves toward him. Then one man takes him, brings him to the apostles, and speaks for him.
Today, the man who helped another one stand. Barnabas.

teach.b: Barnabas wasn't even his first name. Acts introduces him as Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, whom the apostles nicknamed Barnabas, and it translates the name for us. In the Douay-Rheims: "The son of consolation."
Newer translations say son of encouragement. The Greek word behind it, paraklēsis, can mean comfort, encouragement, or an appeal. A nickname like that is given, not chosen.
The first thing we see him do is give: he sells a piece of land and lays the money at the apostles' feet. The second is the scene from the hook.

Saul, later called Paul, comes to Jerusalem after his conversion, and the disciples are afraid of him; they don't believe he is a disciple. Then: "But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles."
He tells them Saul's story, the road, the voice, the bold preaching in Damascus. He puts his own name behind a man nobody trusted.

teach.h: A GOOD MAN, FULL OF FAITH.
teach.b: Later, when the church at Antioch is growing, it's Barnabas they send, and Acts gives him a one-line portrait: "For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith."
And there he goes looking for Saul and brings him to Antioch to teach. Again. Acts is honest that encouragers can disagree.
Barnabas wants to give a young man named John Mark a second chance, after Mark had left them partway through a journey. Paul refuses.
The disagreement is sharp, and they part ways. Barnabas takes Mark anyway. Catholics remember Barnabas as an apostle, though he wasn't one of the Twelve.
His gift was seeing what someone could become, and saying so out loud, before anyone else would.

how: The Church keeps the memorial of Saint Barnabas, Apostle, on 11 June; at Mass the readings come from Acts, where Barnabas is sent out with Saul from Antioch.

o: a Levite title meaning a servant of the Temple
the Aramaic name Saul took after his conversion
the apostles' nickname for Joseph: son of encouragement

the disciples were afraid of him
Barnabas goes to find Saul to teach there
the young man given a second chance

he's called an apostle, but he wasn't one of the Twelve chosen by Jesus in the Gospels.
Acts says they argued sharply over John Mark and went separate ways.
Acts says the apostles gave the name to Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus.

games.q: Saul, who hunted believers, shows up in Jerusalem saying he's changed. the disciples are afraid. you're Barnabas. what do you do?
o: wait until he's proved himself for a few years.
take him to the apostles and tell his story.
warn the others to keep away from him.
games.why: Acts says Barnabas took him, brought him to the apostles, and told how Saul had seen the Lord and preached boldly.

practice: Bring to mind one person others have written off, or someone new and unsure, waiting at the edge of a room, and picture yourself walking over to stand beside them. What good could you honestly say about them?
If you pray, hold them before God as Barnabas held Saul up before the apostles; if you don't, simply keep their good in mind.

wordCard.voice: Barnabas. The apostles' nickname for Joseph of Cyprus, the son of consolation, who brought Saul in when no one else would.

orig.note: Greek: comfort, encouragement, appeal — the word in Barnabas's nickname in Acts 4:36.

carryVoice: Your line: son of encouragement. A nickname like that is earned one person at a time. That's day nine hundred ninety-nine.
